The writer is `_provn_escape_local`. The test gained the row `plain-name_1.x-plain-name_1.x` from test_provn_escaping.py::test_plain_local_parts_unchanged. `encoding_provn_value` of a qualified name returns `'ex:a'`, and of an `Identifier` returns `"http://example.org/b" %% xsd:anyURI` (rows `qualified name` and `identifier`). The test pins that `encoding_provn_value` writes a qualified name through `QualifiedName.provn_representation` and `QualifiedName.provn_bare_representation`, and an identifier through `Identifier.provn_representation` and `_provn_string_literal`, as its docstring states; the bare forms it returned before fail to read back as PROV-N. With the earlier code restored, where `ProvRecord._provn_attribute_block` asked the value for its representation itself and `encoding_provn_value` returned both forms bare, the whole suite fails this test and no other. Removing the check from `encoding_provn_value` alone also fails test_provn_escaping.py::test_provn_writer_lets_an_error_in_a_literal_subclass_propagate and the PROV-N round trips, because the writer now relies on it.

For every BMP character and one astral character, in three positions, a local part that `_PROVN_LOCAL_PERCENT_ENCODED` does not match is escaped by `_provn_escape_local` with backslashes only, so removing them gives the original. A name the model accepts is written without percent-encoding, so a PROV-N reader recovers the same IRI (#524).

For every BMP character and one astral character, in three positions, a local part that `_PROVN_LOCAL_NEEDS_ESCAPE` does not match is returned unchanged by `_provn_escape_local`. The writer's shortcut for a plain local part must never skip a name that needs an escape (#498, PN_LOCAL production [53]).
